video_title: HEATED DEBATE 🔥 Stephen A. & Mad Dog DISAGREE big time on this Knicks question 👀 | First Take

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's contract and leadership built the Knicks' current roster
quotes.excerpt: His willingness to take $100 million less than he could have taken, not only has enabled the Knicks to build out this roster.
quotes.quote: Well, there's a big if in there. They got to win five more games and you'd have to see how Brunson would perform in his first ever Finals, but I do think he would have a potential to be called the greatest Knick. Now, I've been educated by Tony Kornheiser, he's taught me about the 1969-70 Knicks. I'm sure Doggy would as well about how beautiful basketball they played. Frazier and DeBusschere, Bill Bradley, Willis Reed, they had all these Hall of Famers on there. Obviously, the '73 team is legendary and Clyde Frazier can't go anywhere in New York without being worshipped because of those great performances. Earl Monroe. But here's the thing about Brunson in the modern era that can't be passed up, and it's a little bit crude to discuss, but it's so important. I have to bring up his contract. It's not just what Brunson's done on the court for the Knicks. He's been one of the best finishers in the league. His willingness to take $100 million less than he could have taken, not only has enabled the Knicks to build out this roster. The reason they have Bridges and they have Anunoby is because Brunson is taking less money because it's important to him to be an all-time great Knick. He wants to lead them to that championship and he understands the value that is greater than his short-term salary. But also the leadership that he has shown in building the roster. These are his confidants, his friends that he has brought in. One of the things the Knicks have going for them above most teams is their incredible chemistry and Brunson is at the centerpiece of that.

quotes.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson can't surpass Knicks legends like Reed, Frazier, and Ewing
quotes.excerpt: You got to put him ahead of Frazier, Reed, and Ewing? Willis won an MVP.
quotes.quote: That you argue that, but I mean, geez, you got to put him ahead of Frazier, Reed, and Ewing? Willis won an MVP. He made the two biggest shots in the history of the franchise when he made those first two against the Lakers in Game 7. That Knicks team in '69-'70 won 18 in a row and set the consecutive win record. Clyde was, outplayed Jerry West, had 36 points, 19 rebounds, and 12 assists in Game 7 against a team that had Wilt, Baylor, and West, for crying out loud. Three of the top 10 players in the history of the NBA. The second championship team also beat the Lakers, beat the Celtics who had Havlicek and Cowens and people like that. The Knicks, they beat Mobley and Jarrett Allen. Can we calm down just a little bit about Brunson? And he haven't won the Finals yet. They haven't won the Finals yet. To me, you put him in any order you want. Reed, Frazier, Ewing. Those three. You want to put Brunson fourth, even if he wins? I'll give you that. No problem whatsoever. He's not not yet. Am I gonna put him even though Ewing didn't win? He lost to Jordan and Olajuwon. All right? That's who Ewing lost to when he lost in the postseason. Michael Jordan and Olajuwon. I mean, two of the great players, or the best, and a top 15 player in the history of the league and he lost in Game 7 for crying out loud. He is not over those top four. That is not fair. That's blasphemous. Really it is. Silly.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's championship would make him the greatest Knick
quotes.excerpt: If the New York Knicks win a championship with Jalen Brunson, he would be the greatest Knick.
quotes.quote: It's not blasphemous. You have lost your damn mind. Listen, understand the premise of the question. None of this is a conversation if a championship isn't in New York. But if the New York Knicks win a championship with Jalen Brunson, who's averaging 29 on 50% shooting in these conference finals. If this man, by the way, last year in the conference semifinals, who did he beat? He beat Tatum and he beat Jaylen Brown to get to the conference finals. Let's not forget that, okay? So here you are, you arrive in New York four years ago. We're looking at you because we wanted Kevin Durant, okay? We wanted Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving, okay? We got Jalen Brunson. And look at what fools it's made of all of us. Jalen Brunson comes in here, his first year with the New York Knicks, he's averaged 24 and 6. The last three years, 28.7, 26, and 26 a game. The New York Knicks went first round, second round, conference final, Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals, then Game 6 of the Conference Finals. And now, here he is, one game away from the Finals. If he wins the championship, it will either be against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the reigning defending NBA champion Oklahoma City Thunder, or it will be against the new generation led by Victor Wembanyama for the San Antonio Spurs. If he wins a championship, first of all, get Ewing out of there. You didn't deliver it.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's championship would be under more adverse conditions
quotes.excerpt: If this man delivers the chip, it is under far more adverse conditions than what the New York Knicks had to deal with.
quotes.quote: The New York Knicks last chance at a championship was 1994. That's how many years ago is that? We talk about 32 years. And Jalen Brunson brings you a title for the first time in over three decades? I'm sorry. I'm looking at Walt Clyde Frazier, I know he's that dude. You got four other dudes that's on the All-NBA's All-Time 75th Anniversary Team. That's who he was playing with. Who's Brunson playing with? I know they look great now. Mikal Bridges over the last 10 games, he's been phenomenal. Major, major props to him. Josh Hart, you told me to shut up, I shut up. But not long enough to not give them props because Mikal Bridges deserves it, Josh Hart deserves it, OG Anunoby deserves it and the whole bit. But it's about Brunson, okay? If this man delivers the champion, if he delivers the chip, it is under far more adverse conditions than what the New York Knicks had to deal with. He definitely goes atop the list. Number one. Number one. Ahead of everybody.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's teammates compared to Knicks legends
quotes.excerpt: This is not DeBusschere and Bradley and Willis Reed and Earl the Black Jesus, Earl the Pearl Monroe.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
text_blocks.text: How many championships did Reed win? He won two. How many Clyde win? He won two. He's got two for his team.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I just told you they're playing with each other. I just told you they're playing with each other. You got four other dudes you're playing with that's on the NBA's All-75th Anniversary Team.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I love Karl-Anthony Towns. He ain't on that list. OG Anunoby, love him. $212 million, I've never blinked. That linebacker playing forward for the New York Knicks, love OG. Mikal Bridges, very proud of that brother right now, keep it up. Josh Hart, but this is not DeBusschere and Bradley and Willis Reed and Earl the Black Jesus, Earl the Pearl Monroe. That's who his teammate was. Who Brunson has? Who does Brunson have? Are you kidding me? No, out without question. The New York Knicks win the championship this year. Jalen Brunson goes down as the greatest Knick of all time, no disrespect.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
text_blocks.text: Oh my God. You what you have for breakfast? You are playing.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's challenge to win a championship vs. past Knicks' failures
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson delivers a chip to New York City and you think he gets to defer to Ewing? Please.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
text_blocks.text: Ewing lost to Michael Jordan and Olajuwon.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I'm sorry to leave Windy out of the conversation. Doggy, let me ask you this question, Doggy. Now you were doing Mike and the Mad Dog talk radio back then. You all had the number one show in the country. No, listen to me, listen to me. Game 7 in Houston in '94. Who'd you have winning the game?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris "Mad Dog" Russo
text_blocks.text: I thought Houston was going to win.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: They did blow Game 6. They did because they had him in Game 6 and they didn't close. My point to you is this. The Knicks were right there. Ewing was on the court. You had two opportunities to close and you didn't. Jalen Brunson delivers a chip to New York City and you think he gets to defer to Ewing? Please. You sit down. Stay sitting down. It's nothing to discuss. The only person is debatable is Walt Clyde Frazier and even that ain't gonna do it.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Just remember, if he wins a championship, he'll have either beaten Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the best player in the NBA right now back-to-back, or he'll beat Victor Wembanyama, who has a chance to be one of the greatest of all time. Don't forget that because he's got to overcome that and that would be part of the resume.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: That's what I said. That was at the start of my argument. He beats them? Please.
